claim: OUT-006/SCOPE-006 is satisfied by two dependent tasks: TASK-001 adds PortfolioApplication.integrate_ready_change backed by package-owned completion capture, explicit Git-object tree construction, one target CAS, typed Integration attention, and replayable residue cleanup; TASK-002 adds a change-scoped operation that consumes persisted attention by admitting one independently reviewed additive repair commit, advancing the reviewed boundary, clearing matching attention, and re-enabling deterministic Integration retry. Proof is focused package tests over real temporary Git with the candidate-proof dependency replaced only below the public application boundary.
evidence: Owner evidence matches current source: change_workspace.py `integrate`/`_integrate_locked` takes caller-supplied `reviewed_commits`, merges, and CASes the target with no package publication; design_package.py `DesignPackageStore` owns create/read_verified/publish_contract/checkpoint with no completion capture or cleanup; delivery_runtime.py declares `DeliveryFrontier.integration_result_id` and only reads it in `change_stage()`; portfolio_application.py `acquire_frontier_work` only projects `integration_ready_change_ids`. The claimed gap is real and unowned today.

Ownership satisfies COM-010: PortfolioApplication is the sole composition point holding `PortfolioApplicationDependencies(package_store, coordinator, workspace_manager)` plus the change runtimes, so a single atomic product+package CAS (COM-003) cannot be expressed at any narrower owner. No new package or module is introduced, and target_cutover.py is correctly untouched — it owns source-artifact cutover, not branch Integration.

Task decomposition is the smallest safe chain. TASK-001 is large but indivisible under COM-003: splitting capture from publication would either publish package state outside the single CAS or create an intermediate with no observable target boundary. TASK-002 is separable because its writer boundary (accepting an externally reviewed repair commit) is a distinct authority admission, and its dependency on TASK-001 is required because it consumes attention that only TASK-001 publishes.

Acceptance coverage is 1:1 with admitted authority. OUT-006 AC1's five rejection inputs map to TASK-001's stale/pending/mutated/sibling/branch-mismatch attention set; AC2 maps to the product and semantic-only flows over the explicit merge/package tree; AC3 maps to replay cleanup without a second target commit; AC4 maps to conflict/proof/CAS failure recording heads, target, diagnostics, and retry condition with no merge residue; AC5 maps to TASK-002's attention clearance gated on a reviewed single-child commit. No AC is unassigned and no task adds an unadmitted output.

Proof is boundary-valid under h-ac-quality B4: the claimed boundary is the public `integrate_ready_change` / repair operation exercised against real temporary Git repositories, and only the candidate-proof dependency is replaced below that boundary — the same pattern already used by `PortfolioApplicationHooks` for identity and clock. Existing durable coverage (serve/kanban/tests/test_change_workspace.py `test_integration_uses_merge_commit_and_configured_target_cas`, `test_integration_retry_recovers_after_target_cas_before_coordination_update`, `test_integration_conflict_emits_finding_without_advancing_target`) is maintained rather than duplicated, and both tasks name existing test files only — durable-test delta is bounded and consistent with COM-004 and COM-012.

Scope exclusions are correct, not gaps: authority.json places MCP exposure in OUT-007 (dependency_ids include OUT-006) and user-visible resolution in OUT-008, so TASK-001/002 excluding MCP, Cockpit, agents, and prompts respects admitted outcome boundaries rather than dropping required coverage.
